correctness.rationale: The Riemann–Mumford theorem turns the question into the exact action of Sp6(F2) on the 28 and 36 quadratic refinements. The source derives the affine action. Exhaustive generation by symplectic transvections reaches exactly 1451520 distinct group elements, matches the independent known group order, and yields 30 distinct two-permutation spectra. The external group table contains 30 conjugacy classes, so these spectra are exactly classes. Direct fixed-power integer counts distinguish respectively 18, 24 and 30 signatures after one, two and three extensions. Independent eight-branch-point enumeration and irreducible-polynomial existence prove a sharpness collision for real smooth hyperelliptic curves over every odd field. The standalone source and CSV have been extracted and executed.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: A theorem using explicit Galois permutations cannot simply be reversed to prove that six small integer counts suffice. The new group enumeration establishes that inverse direction; explicit smooth hyperelliptic examples prove the lower bound for the number of extensions. A prior six-count hyperelliptic branch-partition theorem implies this statement only on the hyperelliptic subfamily, not for general genus-three curves.

The inspected results give the representations or a method to compute their action for a curve, but do not assert that six counts reconstruct the conjugacy class or prove the sharp three-extension threshold. The sharp hyperelliptic subcase is covered by earlier work; the claim is genuinely broader because it identifies Frobenius for arbitrary genus-three curves and all 30 Sp6(2) types.

value.rationale: For any smooth genus-three curve in odd characteristic, six accessible counts of two intrinsic finite étale theta schemes suffice to reconstruct an entire symplectic level-two Frobenius conjugacy class, with exact universal and realized optimality threshold. This is a natural arithmetic reconstruction and information-loss problem, not an arbitrary small-parameter calculation; it does not assume realization of all abstract group classes. The hyperelliptic special case and its sharpness collision are credited as already known; the new value lies in extending the reconstruction to arbitrary Frobenius types.
